title: Ulterior Motives Detection: Reproducing a Hidden-Goal Detector on a Small Open Model

original_idea.body:
# Ulterior Motives Detection: Reproducing a Hidden-Goal Detector on a Small Open Model

**Problem:** 'Ulterior Motives: Detecting...' (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2604.23460) presents methods to detect hidden goals/motives. Whether the detection approach transfers to small open models that students can run, and how it degrades across goal types, is open.

**Direction:** Set up small open model organisms with in-context hidden goals of varying types (resource acquisition, self-preservation, info-leak). Reimplement the paper's core detection signal (e.g., behavioral probes or response-pattern features) and measure detection AUROC per goal type on a single GPU. Identify which hidden-goal categories are hardest to detect.

**Why it matters:** Hidden-goal detection is central to anti-scheming safety cases. A small-scale reproduction with a per-goal-type breakdown tells the community whether the method is broadly usable or narrowly tuned, without needing frontier models.

**Relevant context:** 'Ulterior Motives: Detecting...' (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2604.23460). Related to in-context scheming model organisms ('Frontier Models are Capable of In-Context Scheming', arXiv:2412.04984) and Petri (Anthropic).
